properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-19 on main 6a45d4b: 23 of the 25 typed edge helpers draw_edges runs dropped a property a bare re-draw left out; only satisfies (#771) and authored_by (roles kept as a set) kept them, and depends_on kept them only when given argued_by, though its field text said a re-draw keeps what it leaves out
properties.statement: Measured with tests/a_redrawn_edge_keeps_what_the_call_leaves_out.rs (MCP in_memory program): for every helper draw_edges runs, draw the edge bare, put a declared property on it the bare call does not name (create_edge with the whole bag), draw it bare again. On main 6a45d4b 23 helpers dropped it: allocate (weight), answers (note), calibrated_against (note), complies_with (evidence), constrains (note), consumes (weight), contains (note), decomposes (note), depends_on (dependency_type; and argued_by, in a second test), deploy_to (status), documents (doc_kind), gate_on (rationale), governed_by (note), invalidates (note), owned_by (note), part_of_flow (weight), provides (weight), realizes (completeness), release_includes (as_checksum), require_resource (criticality), schedule_for (recorded_at), verifies (coverage), violates_rule (rationale; and a confirmed status went back to its default). Not a new cause: the mechanism is the one recorded in fact:revising-a-change-events-affected-list-resets-the-acceptances-already-on-its-changed-edges-2026-10-10 (create_edge replaces the whole bag) and fixed for SATISFIES alone by #771 (DesignGraph::draw_edge_keeping) — this is its recurrence, counted, across every other helper. Fixed: each core typed helper draws through draw_edge_keeping, so one rule holds; the generic create_edge still replaces. Excluded, with reasons in the test: imposes, operates_in, performed_in, pin_at_epoch, precedes (their edges declare no property; performed_in draws through it anyway), move_component and contain_component (they move a child, not re-draw). No Decision in the design says any helper must replace (searched; dec:idea-should-an-edge-write-report-and-preserve-what-it-replaced-the-way-a-node-write-does is open and asks a different question: preserving and reporting a replaced value).
